candidates.summary: Addy Osmani (Claude Code at Anthropic) published an X article, "Your coding agents made you a manager": the skills for managing agents are the skills for managing a team, and you do not need the title. He maps engineering-manager habits onto Claude Code — giving the agent a way to check its work, writing what is not in the repo, compounding corrections in CLAUDE.md, treating hooks as hard requirements, planning before building, and reviewing diffs as if you will get paged for them.
facts: Quote: "Every gripe you have about bad managers is a bug report for interacting with agents."
Quote: "The engineers who get the most out of agents aren't necessarily the ones who are best at prompt engineering. They're the ones who learned how to manage, intentionally or otherwise."
He writes that prompts, CLAUDE.md and skills are requests the model can choose to act on, while hooks, deny rules and managed settings are always enforced.

On Claude Code /batch: it "takes a big mechanical change and creates 5 to 30 tasks, displays the plan, executes them in separate worktrees (separate checkouts of the repo), and creates a PR for each one."
Advice: if two correction attempts fail, start a fresh session with a better prompt; "Review the diff as if you'll get paged for it."
Ryan Carson quoted the gripe/bug-report line and called the article "pure gold."
A related earlier essay on his site is titled "Your AI coding agents need a manager."

related.name: Earlier essay: Your AI coding agents need a manager

candidates.summary: Henry Han's arXiv paper "Enhancing Local and Global Structure in Compressed AI Agent Memory" (2611.08341) says a memory compression that preserves each item's nearest neighbors can still move passages across themes, which matters when agents consolidate, delete or compare memories. The author proposes locality-aware quantization (LAQ), a hinge objective on an OPQ index aimed at the far end of the memory.
facts: Submitted 2026-11-05; author listed as Henry Han.
The paper evaluates local fidelity L at 10 neighbors and global fidelity G at 30 to 50 percent of the memory.
At 96 bytes per passage, "rescored binary codes reach an L of 0.97 yet move 10.1 percent of passages to another theme; PCA with 8-bit codes, at an L of 0.77, moves 1.7 percent."
"Reconstruction alone raises G in 0 of 52 held-out runs; the far hinge raises it in all 52."
"LAQ raises G in all 52 (p=8.5×10^{-4} over 13 memory-encoder groups)", including an external FinDER memory, and "scales to a million passages."

candidates.summary: Lenny Rachitsky published a podcast interview with Tulsee Doshi, head of product for Google's frontier AI models, including Gemini and multimodal models such as Nano Banana, Genie, Veo and Lyria. Public show notes list Google's full-stack frontier AI strategy, what product managers do inside a frontier lab, Doshi's 60-20-20 framework for balancing what works now and what is almost working, and how to write a first eval.
facts: Listed on Lenny's Newsletter on 2026-11-08 (feed timestamp 13:31Z); marked Paid; about 59 minutes.
Subtitle: "Tulsee Doshi on building Google’s frontier models, why evals and vibes both matter, and her 60-20-20 framework for shipping ahead of the curve."

Listed discussion topics include why model development is "not just engineering, but also like Snape’s potions class," Google's full-stack strategy, writing a first eval, and "the rising value of great PMs."
The public page does not spell out the 60-20-20 split beyond "balancing what works now and what’s almost working"; the full transcript is behind the paywall.

candidates.summary: The Verge reports that rights holders of Elvis Presley's music and the publisher of some of Eminem's biggest records are suing AI music company Suno, claiming it illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists. The Presley suit argues Suno violated Tennessee's ELVIS Act, which makes it illegal for an AI company to clone a singer's voice.
facts: Terrence O'Brien, The Verge, 8 November 2026, 5:23 PM UTC.
Presley-suit quote: "Suno has mechanically encoded itself with artists’ identities, hard-work, creativity, and time, and harnessed them all for a consistent conveyor belt of cold hard cash."
The article says the suits closely mirror one filed by Jason Isbell and others in September, which claimed Suno created imitations of the plaintiffs but did not claim copyright infringement directly.

Suno spokesperson Cat McCormack told The Verge: "Suno exists to help people create new, original music, not to trade on anyone’s name or likeness, and we prohibit any unauthorized use of an artist’s work. To protect against this, we do not allow prompts for specific artists’ names and songs and work with third-party providers to screen uploaded audio files and lyrics for potential misuse."
The article says this adds to lawsuits Suno is facing from Sony, UMG, Isbell, Reservoir Media and others.

candidates.summary: Meng To shared an open-source WebGL animation of the MacBook touch background. The repository kubai087/pro-threads is MIT-licensed and described on GitHub as an animated wallpaper of letters woven from threads of light, inspired by the MacBook Pro PROLED XDR wallpaper, with a full A–Z thread typeface, palettes and a live shader.
facts: Meng To, 2026-11-08T15:30:12Z: "open-source animation of the macbook touch background." linking github.com/kubai087/pro-threads.

Original post by Kubai087 on 2026-10-30 described recreating the MacBook Pro PROLED XDR wallpaper in WebGL, then making all 26 letters plus presets, and adding halo, black hole, Möbius-ring and tunnel effects intended for a website hero section.
